title: FITCF: A Framework for Automatic Feature Importance-guided Counterfactual Example Generation

method.decision_and_generator_roles: ZEROCF obtains y_pred and feature attributions from a BERT classifier fine-tuned on the target dataset. An LLM generates edited text from original input, BERT prediction and attributed words. FITCF clusters SBERT embeddings with k-means, selects near-centroid examples, generates ZEROCF edits, and uses the same BERT to remove non-flipping demonstration pairs. More near-centroid examples are selected until the required demonstration count is obtained. The resulting demonstrations plus feature words condition a final few-shot LLM generation.
method.attribution: Gradient, Integrated Gradients, LIME and SHAP via FERRET; special-token words are replaced and subwords merged. The study uses attribution for BERT, not the generative LLM itself.
method.validation: BERT label verification applies to constructed demonstration pairs. The paper does not specify that every final generated counterfactual must be rejected until it passes the same BERT checker.
method.budget_and_stopping: Demonstration count l=2k:10 for AG News,8 for SST2. If too few generated demonstration edits flip BERT, additional near-centroid instances are iteratively selected. No general finite retry guarantee is stated in the method.
method.models: Generation: Llama3-8B, Qwen2.5-32B and Qwen2.5-72B; attribution/demonstration verification: fine-tuned BERT. Qwen versions are GPTQ Int4; experiments use single RTX A6000/A100/H100 depending model.

evaluation.datasets: AG News four-class topic and SST2 binary sentiment. Main experimental N is not clearly supplied in inspected main text; do not infer it from percentages.
evaluation.baselines: Polyjuice, BAE, FIZLE; compare ZEROCF and FITCF variants across four attribution methods.
evaluation.validity_metric: Soft Label Flip Rate (SLFR), any predicted-label change. Section5.1 states same LLM for generation and classification. AppendixG.2 actually prompts the LLM with original+edited input together and asks yes/no whether their predicted categories differ. This paired judgment is not equivalent by definition to independent target-model label calls.
evaluation.quality_metrics: GPT2 perplexity and normalized word-level Levenshtein distance TS (lower is more similar). This TS is lexical edit distance, not semantic similarity. Feature-attribution faithfulness is evaluated through comprehensiveness, sufficiency and Kendall tau with leave-one-out.
evaluation.ablation: Remove important words; reduce demonstration count from2k to k; remove BERT flip verification. More demonstrations generally help SLFR; metric trade-offs vary by task/model.
evaluation.interpretation_caution: Do not repeat a universal outperforming claim: Table1 contains metric/setting exceptions. For example Llama3-8B AGNews SHAP ZEROCF SLFR98.0% versus FITCF94.0%; the table does not show every FITCF variant improving every quantity.
evaluation.human_evaluation: No human plausibility study; explicitly deferred because it requires annotations.

limitations: English-only two-classification-task evaluation; no cross-domain decision-support deployment evidence.
Only BERT predictions used for the attribution/demonstration-verifier role; contribution of other model architectures to those roles is explicitly unexplored.

LLM used for final paired flip judgment differs from BERT used for grounding and demonstration checks. AppendixG.1 assumes similar classifier accuracies imply consistent SLFR tendencies, which is not a proof of per-example agreement.
Fluency and edit distance are not semantic adequacy or real-world actionability.
No study of human trust, audience-adaptation preservation or final natural-language claims.
claim_preservation_overlap: The paper covers attribution-guided counterfactual construction and verified demonstrations, not a multi-audience final explanation renderer. I found no protocol for preserving target-decision claims across novice/expert rewrites or independent auditing of such rendered claims in the inspected method/results/appendices. This is a bounded paper-level observation, not a global novelty claim.
novelty_implication: Attribution-guided counterfactual generation, BERT label-flip filtering, verified few-shot demonstrations and component ablations are established prior art. A thesis keeping the decision LLM fixed must explicitly change attribution/checker access rather than silently adopt cross-model evidence.
baseline_feasibility: Useful algorithmic predecessor. Faithful reproduction needs BERT checkpoint, attribution toolchain, SBERT/k-means demonstration construction and original generator/paired-evaluation prompts. Replacing BERT with the target LLM or replacing paired judgment with independent label calls is an adaptation and must be labelled. Heavy32B/72B variants are optional resource-heavy comparisons;8B still requires GPU resources.

title: iFlip: Iterative Feedback-driven Counterfactual Example Refinement

method.roles: Separate counterfactual generator G and explained classifier M. Initial y=M(x), choose desired y_tilde !=y. Generate x_cf0. If M(x_cf)=y_tilde stop; otherwise iteratively refine with feedback and recheck.
method.models: Generators OLMo2-7B, Qwen3-32B, Llama3.3-70B. Main explained classifiers are task-specific BERT. Additional experiments use RoBERTa. AppendixC.2 tests BERT-to-RoBERTa transfer of candidate edits or feedback, not generativeLLM decision targets.
method.feedback: Explained-model predicted-label maximum softmax confidence; SHAP,AttnLRP,Gradient×Input,LIME important words; LLM natural-language feedback; or combined confidence+SHAP+NL.
method.budget: Formal method allows initial candidate plus up toK refinement steps; experiment setting lists5iterations (with studies up to15). Generation temperature0.9,top-p0.95,top-k50,max-new-tokens4096. Top important words max(10,floor(0.1*original_words)). Explained-model majority voting over512-token windows/stride256.
method.stopping: Early stop after desired target-class success; otherwise stop at maxiterations. No unconditional100%success guarantee. They compare with nofeedback, randomfeedback, least-attributedfeedback and noearlystop.

evaluation.datasets: IMDb, AGNews and SNLI with premise/hypothesis edits separately. Dataset sources given; main per-condition sampleN not clearly established in inspected description, so no per-input rate uncertainty reconstructed.
evaluation.baselines: CGG, FIZLEnaive, Causal What-Ifs. Main Table1 compares generators with BERT as explained model; AppendixC.1 compares RoBERTa.
evaluation.validity_metric: LFR equation counts any label change M(x)!=M(x_cf). This is weaker than formal early-stopping target success M(x_cf)=y_tilde in multiclass tasks. AppendixJ.1 explicitly illustrates undesired NEUTRAL→ENTAILMENT when CONTRADICTION was intended. Report target-success and any-flip separately in thesis.
evaluation.quality_metrics: Sentence embedding cosine similarity using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 is used as minimality proxy; GPT2 perplexity for fluency. Embedding similarity is not a literal minimum-edit or semantic-validity proof.
evaluation.headline_numbers: FullPDF intro/§6.1 reports78.8%relative validity gain with4.95%lower similarity averaged across selected baselines/settings; this differs from officialXML abstract57.8%and is NOT a reproduced result. Prefer table-specific contextual comparisons if citing.
evaluation.user_study: 3 English-proficient participants evaluate10randomAGNews source examples under3methods (CGG,FIZLE,iFlip-NL) with6pointLikert completeness,overall satisfaction,feasibility. Reported human means e.g overall satisfaction2.67,2.93,5.13 respectively; tiny complementary study, not general evidence of appropriate reliance.
evaluation.judge_study: Gemma3-27B,GPT-OSS-120B,DeepSeek-R1 rate same subjective dimensions; LLM-judge alignment is not independent task correctness.
evaluation.cost: Table6 hardware: OLMo2-7B1×V10032GB;Qwen3-32B1×H10080GB;Llama3.3-70B2×H10080GB. Table7 AGNews OLMo2 confidence7.30h vsNL17.90h for reported run; sample denominator is not established here, so do not derive per-case latency.
evaluation.additional_tests: CDA training and ID/OOD/human-CF tests; no general consistency guarantee, with some NLI outcomes worse than baseline. Early stopping prevents later candidate flip-backs. Trade-offs and random/least-attributed controls already in paper.

limitations: English-only; limited attribution-method set; expensive iterative generation, especially NL feedback.
3-person10-case user study is explicitly limited; satisfaction/feasibility ratings do not measure human decision correctness or calibrated trust.
Main targets are BERT/RoBERTa rather than instruction-tuned generativeLLM decisions, despite LLM generators.
Any-flip reporting and desired-target stopping are distinct success definitions.
Cosine similarity and PPL do not establish complete semantic adequacy or real-world actionability.

Isolated appendix consistency issues: Table33 labels originalbusiness/counterfactualbusiness but isFlipYes; another row business→sport but isFlipNo. AppendixL introductory dimension names differ from its detailed scoring definitions. These are reporting/protocol-document inconsistencies to check before reuse, not proof that whole experiments are invalid.
claim_preservation_overlap: The paper validates edited inputs and rates their explanatory quality; it does not implement/test an audience-adapted natural-language explanation layer preserving claims from a fixed decision-evidence record. I found no novice/expert rewrite comparison or final-claim preservation audit. However, confidence/attribution/NLfeedback, target-class checks,earlystop,randomfeedback controls, budgets and failure examples already overlap prospective supporting components.
novelty_implication: A bounded feedback+earlystopping CF loop, sensitivity to important words, validity/similarity/cost trade-off, and transfer tests cannot be claimed new. The main decision-model boundary should be explicit; applying to generativeLLM targets requires an actual justified adaptation and evidence.
baseline_feasibility: Confidence-only and NLfeedback versions are implementable candidates but currently trained-classifier-target baselines. Whitebox attribution needs gradient/attention access.8B/7B generator variants still GPUheavy;32B/70B models are not essential to a bounded thesis pilot. Budget-matched comparisons must account for initial generation, feedback and retries. No code executed.

title: Truth or Twist? Optimal Model Selection for Reliable Label Flipping Evaluation in LLM-based Counterfactuals

method.scope: Studies semantic/ground-truth label validity for counterfactual data augmentation (CDA), explicitly distinguished from explaining a particular model by changing its prediction (p1footnote2).
method.generator_judge_roles: Counterfactuals generated by FIZLE or FLARE with Llama3-{8B,70B}/Qwen2.5-{14B,32B}. Judges grouped as same model, same family, independent with/without target-data fine-tuning, or distillation-related;15judges including trainedBERT/RoBERTa and multiple off-the-shelfLLMs, plus majority ensemble.
method.evaluator_protocol: Judge assigns a class to the edited input using a direct category-only task prompt (AppendixD/Fig10). LFR compares edited-input predicted label against ORIGINAL DATASET label. It is not the paired original+edited yes/no meta-judgment shown in FitCF AppendixG.
method.human_alignment: Human-label edited inputs define semantic reference labels; compare automatic and human aggregate LFR via absolute closeness/rank, most-to-least alignment ratio and Pearson correlation. This evaluates semantic label agreement, not access to model-internal reasoning.

evaluation.datasets: AGNews,SST2,SNLI. User study90nativeEnglishannotators;45sourceindices sampled/dataset;eachsubset evaluated by2annotators,authorsadjudicateties;15counterfactuals/annotator described. Reported Cohen kappa0.55 (moderateagreement). Do not reconstruct a unique totalannotation count fromthese summaries.
evaluation.main_result: Authors report independent non-fine-tuned judges align best on average with humanLFR, but substantial discrepancy remains; ordinary downstream taskperformance does not guarantee label-flipjudge alignment. Their aggregate best relationship ranking4.15/Pearson0.47 are experiment-specific, not guarantee of anyindependentjudge.
evaluation.augmentation: CDA uses500originaltraininginstances plus generatedcounterfactuals, classifiertrainedforCDA distinct fromfine-tunedjudgecheckpoint. Evaluates originaltestsets andhumanlabelledCFset, excludesselectedCFs/originals fromtraining. AppendixH reports moderateSpearmancorrelation0.41forAGNews betweenrelationshipranking andCFtestperformance;weak onotherdatasets.
evaluation.important_boundary: A semantic judge can disagree with the targetmodel while being morehuman-aligned. Its independentjudgment cannot replace reclassification with the fixed targetLLM when testing behavioralCF validity.

limitations: Observed model-relationship associations do not isolate a causal effect of independence, finetuning or contamination; models differ in capability and training.
Human labels for ambiguous editedtext have onlymoderateagreement and adjudication;call them annotatedreference labelsratherthanunquestionabletruth.
The claim of fully automatedCDA inadequacy is limited to studiedsystems/settings. No theorem that all automationis impossible.
claim_preservation_overlap: Supplies strong prior art for evaluating the evaluator and distinguishing humansemantic validCFs fromtargetmodelbehavior. It doesnot provide an audience rewriting layer or claim-level preservation protocol. It narrows any purported novel independent-verifier argument.
novelty_implication: Judge-selection effects, weak human/model alignment and the distinction semantic-validity vsbehavioralflip are existing research insights. Thesis should retain BOTH constructs if relevant ratherthaninventingthisdistinction or equatingindependentjudgeagreementwithfaithfulness.
baseline_feasibility: Use as evaluation-design foundation; reproducingall4generators×15judges isresourceheavyandunnecessaryforpilot. A limited clearlylabelled independentsemanticcheck mayaugment same-targetreclassification, withhumanannotationonfeasiblesubset. No authors codeexecuted.
